messages:
maya: heads up — the int4 canary we rolled to raven-lite this morning is spiking structured-output parse failures on funcalls. noticed a pattern with small kv-prefixes + batching enabled. attaching short traces below :frowning:

jon: ack. can you paste a minimal example of the request + response you saw?

maya: sure. simple toolcall prompt, model returns JSON but with interleaved prefix remnants:

maya: ```
User: create_task(title=\"Summarize Q1 report\")
Model: {\"action\": \"create_task\", \"args\": {\"title\": \"Summarize Q1 report\"}}
...prefix:start:kv-12\\n{\\\"action\\\": \\\"noop\\\"}\\n...prefix:end
```

sasha: that looks like kv-cache leakage into streaming chunks — maybe the prefix sentinel wasn't filtered before streaming write. do we see this only on int4?

maya: mostly on int4 canaries — int8 runs are clean. reproduction matrix:
- raven-lite int4 canary (batching=on, kv-prefixing=on) -> ~2.8% parse-fail on funcalls
- raven-lite int8 (same config) -> ~0.03%
- dedicated q4_0 (no batching) -> ~0.01%

li: interesting. could be kernel reordering causing chunk boundary to include leftover kvcache flush metadata. any streaming boundary logs?

maya: pasted one raw stream from the canary: non-essential fields redacted:

maya: ```
STREAM_CHUNK 0: {\"token\":\"{\",\"id\":321}
STREAM_CHUNK 1: {\"token\":\"\"action\"\",\"id\":322}
STREAM_CHUNK 2: {\"token\":\":\",\"id\":323}
STREAM_CHUNK 3: {\"token\":\"\"create_task\"\",\"id\":324}
STREAM_CHUNK 4: {\"token\":\"}\n...prefix:start:kv-12\",\"id\":325}
STREAM_CHUNK 5: {\"token\":\"{\",\"id\":326}
STREAM_CHUNK 6: {\"token\":\"\"action\"\",\"id\":327}
STREAM_CHUNK 7: {\"token\":\"\":\"noop\"}\" ,\"id\":328}
```

jon: ugh. fs-layer or runtime-level prefix markers leaking into token stream. did the canary use continuous-batching optimization?

maya: yes continuous-batching = true. when I flipped batching->false the spike went away in a small A/B run.

sasha: quick mitigation options:
- add stream filter to drop tokens matching regex /\.\.\.prefix:start:kv-\d+/ before parse (cheap, defensive)
- tighten streaming sentinel in runtime so those markers are never emitted to the client
- in parse layer, expand resilient JSON heuristics (strip trailing noise after a valid top-level object)

li: I worry about relying on regex strip — could mask other bugs. but as a short roll-forward that's acceptable for hosted canary traffic. longer term need to patch runtime.

maya: ran a short patch with streaming filter in front of the parser for canary (only enabled for raven-lite int4). after ~3k calls failures dropped from 2.8% -> 0.12%. bad cases now are truncated payloads rather than marker interleave.

infra-bot: deploy noted — filter-proxy v2026.03.18-rc1 rolled to raven-lite-int4 canary (traffic 2%).

jon: nice. can you share the exact filter snippet so eng-runtime can adopt canonical fix?

maya: pasted minimal filter used in the proxy:```python
# drop simple kv-prefix markers that leaked into stream
import re
PREFIX_RE = re.compile(r"\.\.\.prefix:start:kv-\\d+")
def sanitize_chunk(chunk_text):
    return PREFIX_RE.sub("", chunk_text)
```

sasha: also added a parse-rescue that tries to json.load(prefix-stripped) then if fail, runs a heuristic to take the first balanced {...} block. reduced noise considerably.

li: can we get a root-cause repro deterministically? maybe a low-level test that forces concurrent kvcache flush + batch boundary. I'm going to spin a microbench that toggles kvcache flush between tokens and triggers continuous batching.

maya: test harness would help. I also captured token alignment when running with token-level debug flag: attaching a short dump showing asynchronous write order.

maya: ```
[DBG] kvflush start (thread=12)
[DBG] write chunk id=325 (batch=4)
[DBG] kvflush payload emitted
[DBG] write chunk id=326 (batch=4)
```

jon: that ordering suggests flush triggered in middle of batch emission. runtime should either fully serialize flush events or buffer them off-stream.

sasha: short-term plan proposed:
1) keep streaming regex filter in proxy for raven-lite-int4 canary (done)
2) runtime patch to buffer kvflush metadata until all active batch streams flush (owner: eng-runtime, PR wip)
3) expand parser heuristics as fallback for hosted (low-cost)
4) add unit test simulating concurrent kvflush+batch boundary in kernel tests (owner: eng-ml infra)

li: I created a minimal issue in runtime board and linked the test plan. I'll add deterministic repro steps with the microbench once I finish.

maya: rollout note: we can gradually re-enable continuous-batching after runtime patch; until then keep int4 canary throttled.

jon: thanks — can we add an eval to ensure structured-output compliance (strict funcall JSON pass rate) as a canary metric going forward? ideally alert if >0.5% regression vs baseline.

maya: yes I wired a nightly eval that runs 5k sample toolcall prompts across quant variants and publishes pass rates to the console. added alert rule threshold for >0.5% drop.

sasha: perfect. follow-up: once runtime PR is merged let's run a 10k-run regression for int4 to validate no new edgecases.

maya: agreed. will post results here when I have them. thanks all :thumbsup:

jon: :eyes:
